On-Chain Operator. Lesson 7.7, DEX & liquidity analytics. Navy and cyan. One idea at a time. You write it down. Education only.
You can already read a token's supply and a protocol's fees. Analytics is how you check those claims on the ledger itself.
TVL can double count and moves with token prices.
Depth: the price impact for a given trade size.
Volume/TVL: rough capital turnover; higher means more fees per dollar (Lesson 2.3).
Liquidity migration: incentives move liquidity quickly between pools and chains.
Work the example on paper. Pool A: $50M TVL, $5M daily volume (0.1 turnover). Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.
Work the example on paper. Pool B: $10M TVL, $8M volume (0.8 turnover). Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.
Work the example on paper. B pays LPs far more per dollar, but a $1M trade will move B's price much more than A's. Stamp it Example. It is not a level to copy onto a live position.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Depth checked at my trade size. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
On the checklist, this line has to be true in writing: Volume/TVL used for LP fee estimates. If you cannot write it, the line is open.
Check yourself. 1. Why is depth more useful than TVL for traders? The answer: It measures price impact at a given size.
Check yourself. 2. High volume/TVL means? The answer: More fees per dollar of liquidity.
Check yourself. 3. What causes liquidity migration? The answer: Incentives moving between pools and chains.
By the end of this lesson, you'll be able to measure whether a pool can actually absorb your trade and pay you as an L.P..
